record.paper_title: Structural results on circular-arc graphs and circle graphs: A survey and the main open problems
record.original_question: Characterize, by forbidden induced subgraphs, which claw-free graphs are circular-arc graphs. A claw is the complete bipartite graph K1,3, a claw-free graph contains no induced claw, and a circular-arc graph is an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle. As a starting subcase, determine the forbidden induced subgraph characterization for circular-arc graphs among graphs whose largest stable set has size at most two, where a stable set is a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices.

evidence.quote: characterize circular-arc graphs within the class of claw-free graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A *claw* is the complete bipartite graph $K_{1,3}$, and a graph is *claw-free* if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to the claw. A *circular-arc graph* is the intersection graph of a family of open arcs on a circle. A *stable set* (independent set) in a graph is a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices; the *stability number* $\alpha(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a stable set in $G$.

(a) Determine an explicit list $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs such that a claw-free graph $G$ is a circular-arc graph if and only if $G$ contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to any member of $\mathcal{F}$. Equivalently, characterize by forbidden induced subgraphs the circular-arc graphs within the class of claw-free graphs.

(b) As a starting subcase, give such a forbidden induced subgraph characterization restricted to graphs $G$ with $\alpha(G) \le 2$: describe the minimal list of forbidden induced subgraphs whose absence from a graph with stability number at most $2$ is equivalent to being a circular-arc graph.
artifact.status_search_result: A general forbidden induced subgraph characterization of circular-arc graphs (even restricted to claw-free graphs) remains open. Partial results exist for special subclasses: long circular interval graphs, Helly/proper Helly circular-arc graphs, claw-free chordal graphs, P4-free, paw-free, diamond-free, and split graphs have known forbidden-subgraph characterizations, but the claw-free case in full generality is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Claw-free Graphs. III. Circular interval graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of long circular interval graphs by excluded induced subgraphs (claw, net, antinet, (1,1,1)-prism, plus dominating hole conditions).
status_evidence.claim: Only a subclass (long circular interval graphs) of claw-free graphs related to circular-arc graphs has a known forbidden-subgraph characterization.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Circular-arc Graphs: I. Split Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work characterizing circular-arc graphs within split graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs, indicating the general problem is still under active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Forbidden induced subgraph characterizations of circular-arc graphs are being established class-by-class, suggesting the global/claw-free case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Circular-arc graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: No characterization of circular-arc graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs is currently known.
status_evidence.claim: No general forbidden induced subgraph characterization of circular-arc graphs is known.
